description: POST /api/v1/calculator — one-machine home/small-business profitability with the same solar/battery/grid leftover-watt model as the site. Required: hashrate, power, algorithm, elecCost. Optional: solarW, batteryCapacity, zipCode, powerSources. Example: 3 kW miner on solar by day, grid at $0.15/kWh at night → power=3000, elecCost=0.15, solarW=<array watts>, powerSources={solar:true, battery:false, grid:true} (add batteryCapacity and battery:true to store leftover sun). Returns dailyProfit, dailyCost, solarSavings, runtimeHours, effectiveElecCost. Figures are MinerYield model estimates from live market inputs: estimates only, not investment, financial, or tax advice, and not ROI guarantees. Results vary with network difficulty, coin price, power cost, and hardware performance. Do your own research.

algorithm.description: Catalog algorithm name as stored on MinerYield (SHA-256, Scrypt, KHeavyHash, Eaglesong, SHA512256d, Blake2B, Blake2B-Sia, Blake2B-SHA3, Blake256R14, X11, Cuckatoo31, Cuckatoo32, Equihash, RandomX, SHA3X, Ethash4G, Blake3, zkSNARK, Kadena, NexaPow, XPHash).

batteryCapacity.description: Battery storage in kWh (20 = 20 kWh). Only used when powerSources.battery is true (passing batteryCapacity without powerSources turns battery on). Excess daytime solar charges the battery; the battery covers night hours before grid.

elecCost.description: Grid electricity price in USD per kWh (0.15 = 15 cents). Applied only to leftover watts after solar and battery. There is no separate day/night rate: solar covers the sun window, grid covers the rest at this price.

hardwareCost.description: Upfront hardware cost in USD used for estimated payback days.

hashrate.description: Hashing power (TH/s for SHA-256, MH/s for Scrypt; same units as the catalog).

power.description: Miner wall power in Watts (3000 = 3 kW). Used with solar/battery/grid to compute leftover watts and runtime.

powerSources.description: Which legs of the site calculator to use. solar=true uses solarW during Peak Sun Hours; battery=true uses leftover solar stored in batteryCapacity at night; grid=true keeps the miner running 24h on leftover grid kWh. solar=true + grid=true + battery=false is "solar by day, grid at night". If grid=false the miner only runs while solar or battery energy lasts (runtimeHours < 24).

battery.description: Use leftover daytime solar stored in batteryCapacity to cover night hours.

grid.description: Draw leftover kWh from the grid at elecCost so the miner can run 24 hours. Off = solar/battery-only runtime.

solar.description: Use the solar array (solarW) during Peak Sun Hours. Turn on for any home-solar scenario.

preferredCoin.description: Target coin when an algorithm supports more than one (BTC/BCH/QUAI, SC/BTCB2, BTCB2/SC, ZEC/ARRR, ETC/OCTA/ETHW/QKC, DCR/SCP). Blake2B-SHA3 is HNS only; Cuckatoo31 is MWC only; Cuckatoo32 is GRIN only. Scrypt reports LTC/DOGE (merged). When omitted, the most profitable supported coin is used except Ethash4G, which defaults to ETC.

solarW.description: Home/small-business solar array capacity in Watts (10000 = 10 kW). Used with Peak Sun Hours from zipCode. Solar generation is treated as free during the sun window; leftover watts can charge the battery.

zipCode.description: 5-digit US ZIP for Peak Sun Hours. Defaults to the API-key owner profile, then a server default. Needed for a realistic solar-by-day estimate.
